page.layout: One printed page, one text column at full width. Running head at top: "CAP. III." at left and "ILLUSTRATUS." centred, page number at top right. Below the running text: a rule, then a centred title block (INTRODUCTIO / Ad Canticum / PROPHETÆ / Euticum : quod continetur Cap. III.), then a section heading "I. Titulus hujus Sermonis.", then one paragraph with a woodcut initial and a Hebrew word at the end. Small section mark "§. 1." in the left margin. Catchword in Hebrew at bottom right, below the last line.

main_text.p: tis Regis & palatii ejus; quæ ad reverentiam vocat, & ad studium sanctitatis; quoniam eo ipso constat in cœtu justorum non admitti & consistere non posse profanos, ab aditu ad Regem sanctum, & ingressu in templum sanctum arcendos. Qui proin videbunt Regem manifestatum in palatio sanctitatis suæ; illi judicium ejus verentes non poterunt non semel illi subjicere cum abnegatione sapientiæ omnis carnalis, & condemnatione concupiscentiarum adversus regnum ejus insurgentium, in quibus verum consistit à facie Domini silen-tium.
main_text.head: INTRODUCTIO Ad Canticum PROPHETÆ Euticum : quod continetur Cap. III.
I. Titulus hujus Sermonis.
main_text.p: §. 1.Sequitur jam novus (qui & ultimus) Prophetæ sermo, qui quo ad genus orationis vocatur תפלה, id est oratio, seu supplicatio Habakuci Prophetæ. Claudit itaque Prophæta visionem suam, divinitus acceptam, & hactenus descriptam, sermone votivo, ad Deum directo, quem calidis votis hic compellat. Vox תפלה

page.notes: The Hebrew word תפלה printed at the right below the last line is treated as the catchword; it could also be a marginal Hebrew gloss, but it stands below the text block, so it is read as catchword. The woodcut initial S is joined to "equitur". "tis" at the top is a fragment of a word continued from the previous page. "in palatio" shows a small mark between the two words, read as a space. The Hebrew word after "Vox" is printed on the line below and is transcribed inline. The word "Prophæta" is read with æ as printed; the first "Prophetæ" is read with plain e.
